candidate_095.name: reproduce-before-ablate attribution gate
candidate_095.mechanism_hypothesis: Do not grant a scientific mechanism or agent component causal credit from a system-level gain until the claimed baseline is reproduced end-to-end under the official evaluation and isolated component mutations are then tested against that reproduced baseline with verifiable artifacts.

primary_evidence.source: AblateCell: A Reproduce-then-Ablate Agent for Virtual Cell Repositories, arXiv:2604.19606v2.
primary_evidence.design: The agent first auto-configures the repository, resolves dependencies/data issues and reruns official evaluations while emitting artifacts; only after reproduction does it build a graph of isolated repository mutations and adaptively choose ablation experiments under an impact-versus-cost reward.
primary_evidence.result: Across three single-cell perturbation repositories (CPA, GEARS, BioLORD), AblateCell reports 88.9% end-to-end workflow success, +29.9 percentage points versus the human-expert baseline, and 93.3% accuracy in recovering ground-truth critical components, +53.3 percentage points versus the heuristic baseline.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This is directly aligned with the AdsMind attribution correction from candidate_093: full-system superiority does not identify which internal mechanism caused the gain. Reproduce-first plus isolated ablation is a stronger evidential gate for component credit than reading a nominal architecture or comparing Full only against an open-loop baseline.
primary_evidence.limits: The evaluation is on three computational virtual-cell repositories, not a physical wet lab. The abstract-level evidence does not isolate the causal contribution of the reproduce-first stage versus the mutation-graph search stage, so treat this as system-level support for the attribution workflow rather than a matched ablation of the gate itself.

revocable_repair_support.source: SpaceMind: A Modular and Self-Evolving Embodied Vision-Language Agent Framework for Autonomous On-orbit Servicing, arXiv:2604.14399 plus official author repository summary.
revocable_repair_support.result: SpaceMind converts episode outcomes into persistent skill mutations that can create, rewrite or disable strategies and passes proposed mutations through a quality/safety gate before reuse. In its self-evolution study, four of six groups recover after a single failed episode, including a complete-failure group reaching 100% success and an inspection score improving from 12 to 59. The same codebase transfers to a physical robot with 100% rendezvous success in the reported real-world validation.
revocable_repair_support.interpretation: This is useful cross-domain support for persistent repair memory being editable rather than additive-only, which is directionally consistent with the need to avoid irreversible FORBID-style lockout. It is not yet the requested matched science-domain ablation showing a false constraint being explicitly revoked and the lost optimum recovered.
revocable_repair_support.scope_guard: Do not treat this robotics result as direct evidence that revocable scientific search constraints improve discovery yield; use it only as mechanism-supporting evidence while continuing the matched autonomous-science search.
